words.enDefinition: An interview focused on what someone did in past situations

examples.en: In the behavioral interview, I described how I handled a disagreement at work.
examples.zh: 在「行为面试」中，我描述了自己如何处理工作中的一次分歧。

examples.en: The adviser ran a short behavioral interview using examples from my campus jobs.
examples.zh: 顾问参考我的校内工作经历，组织了一场简短的「行为面试」。

words.enDefinition: An interview asking how someone would respond to hypothetical work situations

examples.en: During the situational interview, I explained what I would do if instructions conflicted.
examples.zh: 在「情境面试」中，我说明了如果指令有冲突，我会怎么做。

examples.en: The practice situational interview used a scenario about two clients needing help at once.
examples.zh: 这场模拟「情境面试」设定了两位客户同时需要帮助的场景。

words.enDefinition: An interview assessing specific abilities through evidence from a candidate's experience

examples.en: Each question in the competency-based interview focused on a skill from the job description.
examples.zh: 这场「胜任力面试」的每道题都围绕职位描述中的一项能力。

examples.en: The workshop used a competency-based interview to assess teamwork and communication separately.
examples.zh: 讲座通过「胜任力面试」分别评估团队合作和沟通能力。

words.enDefinition: An interview exploring tasks someone enjoys and naturally does well

examples.en: The strengths-based interview explored which aspects of my campus job I found most rewarding.
examples.zh: 「优势导向面试」探讨了校内工作中哪些方面最让我觉得有收获。

examples.en: The adviser used a strengths-based interview to ask which activities gave me energy.
examples.zh: 顾问通过「优势导向面试」，询问我做什么事会感到有干劲。

words.enDefinition: An interview using standard questions and scoring to compare candidates

examples.en: In our structured interview practice, every student answered the same questions in order.
examples.zh: 练习「结构化面试」时，每位学生都依次回答同一组问题。

examples.en: The structured interview used the same rating scale for everyone who applied.
examples.zh: 这场「结构化面试」对所有应聘者使用相同的评分标准。

words.enDefinition: An interview where several people question one candidate together

examples.en: The panel interview included two supervisors and someone from the training team.
examples.zh: 这场「多面试官面试」有两位主管和一位培训团队成员参加。

examples.en: During the panel interview, one person asked questions while the others took notes.
examples.zh: 在「多面试官面试」中，一人提问，其他人记笔记。

words.enDefinition: An interview in which multiple candidates are assessed together

examples.en: At the group interview, four applicants discussed how front desk shifts might be divided.
examples.zh: 在「多应聘者面试」中，四名应聘者讨论了如何安排前台轮班。

examples.en: Our group interview ended with an opportunity for each applicant to ask a question.
examples.zh: 「多应聘者面试」结束前，每位应聘者都有机会提一个问题。

collocations: take part in a group interview

words.enDefinition: A practice session that imitates a real job interview

examples.en: My roommate ran a mock interview before I applied for the campus library job.
examples.zh: 申请校图书馆的工作前，室友给我做了场「模拟面试」。

examples.en: The mock interview showed me how often I rushed through the end of an answer.
examples.zh: 这次「模拟面试」让我发现，自己经常匆匆结束回答。

collocations: get feedback after a mock interview

words.enDefinition: An interview involving one interviewer speaking with one candidate

examples.en: I had a one-on-one interview with the person who supervised the evening shift.
examples.zh: 我和负责晚班的主管进行了一场「一对一面试」。

examples.en: Our one-on-one interview covered the same topics we had discussed in the group session.
examples.zh: 这场「一对一面试」涉及我们在小组环节谈过的同样话题。

collocations: a one-on-one interview with a manager

words.enDefinition: A job meeting where the participants are physically in the same place

examples.en: At the in-person interview, I met the staff members who would supervise my placement.
examples.zh: 在「现场面试」中，我见到了将指导我实习的员工。

examples.en: My in-person interview began with a tour of the student services office.
examples.zh: 我的「现场面试」从参观学生服务办公室开始。

words.enDefinition: The last interview in a sequence for a particular job

examples.en: My final-round interview focused on what I wanted to learn during the placement.
examples.zh: 我的「最后一轮面试」主要谈了实习期间我想学到什么。

examples.en: At the final-round interview, I met the person who managed the whole department.
examples.zh: 在「最后一轮面试」中，我见到了整个部门的负责人。

words.enDefinition: The group of people who question and assess a candidate together

examples.en: One member of the interview panel worked in the office I hoped to join.
examples.zh: 「面试官小组」里有一位成员就在我希望加入的办公室工作。

examples.en: I thanked the interview panel before leaving the room and collecting my bag.
examples.zh: 离开房间去取包之前，我向「面试官小组」道了谢。

collocations: a member of the interview panel

words.enDefinition: One person who sits on a group assessing candidates

examples.en: A second panel member asked how I handled competing requests at the library.
examples.zh: 另一位「面试小组成员」问我在图书馆如何处理互相冲突的请求。

examples.en: One panel member wanted to hear from me about the exhibition project.
examples.zh: 一位「面试小组成员」希望听我讲讲那个展览项目。

words.enDefinition: The way an interview is organized and carried out

examples.en: The interviewer explained the interview format before moving on to the first question.
examples.zh: 面试官先说明了「面试形式」，然后开始问第一道题。

examples.en: Our adviser showed how the interview format affects the kinds of answers expected.
examples.zh: 顾问说明了「面试形式」怎样影响面试官对答案的预期。

words.enDefinition: The first question used to start an interview or discussion

examples.en: The opening question was about how I became interested in the museum sector.
examples.zh: 「开场问题」问的是我怎么对博物馆行业产生兴趣的。

examples.en: I gave a short answer to the opening question before we discussed my experience.
examples.zh: 我们谈我的经历之前，我简短回答了「开场问题」。

words.enDefinition: A question about how someone might respond in an imagined situation

examples.en: The hypothetical question involved two colleagues asking me for help at the same time.
examples.zh: 这道「假设性问题」设定两位同事同时找我帮忙。

examples.en: I asked for one detail before answering the hypothetical question about a late delivery.
examples.zh: 在回答有关交货延迟的「假设性问题」前，我先问了一个细节。

words.enDefinition: A question asking for an example of someone's past actions

examples.en: The behavioral question asked for an example of a disagreement with a colleague.
examples.zh: 这道「行为面试题」要求举例描述与同事意见不合的经历。

examples.en: I used my student job to answer a behavioral question about giving feedback.
examples.zh: 我用校内工作经历回答了一道关于如何给反馈的「行为面试题」。

words.enDefinition: A question designed to assess a particular job-related ability

examples.en: The competency-based question on planning asked how I had managed several deadlines.
examples.zh: 那道关于规划能力的「胜任力面试题」问我怎样兼顾多个截止日期。

examples.en: I chose an example from the lab for the competency-based question on communication.
examples.zh: 回答有关沟通能力的「胜任力面试题」时，我选了实验室里的一个例子。

words.enDefinition: A question aimed at getting more detail or uncovering someone's reasoning

examples.en: A probing question prompted me to explain why I had changed the plan.
examples.zh: 一个「深入追问」让我解释了为什么要改变计划。

examples.en: I paused when the interviewer asked a probing question about my personal contribution.
examples.zh: 面试官就我的个人贡献提出一个「深入追问」时，我停顿了一下。

collocations: a probing question about the outcome

words.enDefinition: A question worded to suggest the answer someone should give

examples.en: Our tutor turned a leading question into one that allowed more than one answer.
examples.zh: 导师把一个「引导性问题」改成了可以有多种回答的问题。

examples.en: The adviser pointed out how the leading question suggested a preferred response.
examples.zh: 顾问指出了这个「引导性问题」是怎样暗示期待的答案的。

words.enDefinition: A single question that asks about several related points

examples.en: I wrote down two words to remember each part of the multi-part question.
examples.zh: 我记下两个词，提醒自己别漏答「多部分问题」中的任何一部分。

examples.en: The multi-part question asked what I did and what changed afterward.
examples.zh: 这道「多部分问题」问我做了什么，以及之后有什么变化。

words.enDefinition: A statement or instruction inviting someone to respond in an interview

examples.en: The interview prompt asked me to describe a time I changed my approach.
examples.zh: 这条「面试答题提示」让我讲一次自己调整做法的经历。

examples.en: I read the interview prompt again before choosing a story about a project.
examples.zh: 我又读了一遍「面试答题提示」，才选了一个项目经历来讲。

words.enDefinition: Written observations or reminders made during or about an interview

examples.en: After our practice session, my adviser shared the interview notes she had taken.
examples.zh: 模拟面试结束后，顾问把她记的「面试笔记」给我看。

examples.en: I read my interview notes to recall the question I wanted to practice again.
examples.zh: 我翻看「面试笔记」，想起了自己还想再练习的那个问题。

words.enDefinition: A guide describing how different levels of performance will be rated

examples.en: The mock interview used a scoring rubric with separate scores for each answer.
examples.zh: 这次模拟面试用「评分细则」给每个回答单独打分。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how to read a scoring rubric before we assessed sample answers.
examples.zh: 我们给示例答案评分之前，导师解释了怎样读「评分细则」。

words.enDefinition: Comments on what went well or could improve in an interview

examples.en: My interview feedback mentioned that my examples were clear but sometimes too long.
examples.zh: 「面试反馈」说我举的例子很清楚，但有时讲得太长。

examples.en: I compared the interview feedback from two practice sessions at the careers center.
examples.zh: 我比较了就业中心两次模拟面试给出的「面试反馈」。

words.enDefinition: A prompt inviting a short introduction to a candidate's background

examples.en: When the interviewer said, "Tell me about yourself," I began with my current degree.
examples.zh: 面试官让我「介绍一下自己」时，我先说了自己正在读的学位。

examples.en: We practiced how to respond to "Tell me about yourself," starting with our most recent experience.
examples.zh: 我们练习怎样回答「请介绍一下自己」，从最近的经历讲起。

collocations: a response to "Tell me about yourself."

words.enDefinition: A request to explain relevant past roles or activities in sequence

examples.en: The interviewer said "Walk me through your experience." I began with my campus job.
examples.zh: 听到「请梳理一下你的经历」后，我先从校内工作讲起。

examples.en: The prompt "Walk me through your experience" gave me room to explain why I switched roles.
examples.zh: 「请梳理一下你的经历」这道题让我有机会说明自己为什么换了岗位。

collocations: begin with "Walk me through your experience."
a response to "Walk me through your experience."

words.expression: what interests you about this role
words.lemma: what interests you about this role
words.enDefinition: A question about which parts of a role appeal to someone
acceptedEnVariants: what interests you about this role

examples.en: When I heard "What interests you about this role?", I mentioned the chance to work with visitors.
examples.zh: 听到「这个岗位哪里吸引你」时，我提到了与来访者打交道的机会。

examples.en: I practiced answering "What interests you about this role?" without repeating the whole job description.
examples.zh: 练习回答「这个岗位哪里吸引你」时，我尽量避免重复整个职位描述。

collocations: ask "What interests you about this role?"
a response to "What interests you about this role?"
practice answering "What interests you about this role?"

words.expression: why do you want to work here
words.lemma: why do you want to work here
words.zhGloss: 你为什么想在这里工作
words.enDefinition: A question asking what draws someone to a particular employer
acceptedZhAnswers: 你为什么想在这里工作
acceptedEnVariants: why do you want to work here

examples.en: My answer to "Why do you want to work here?" mentioned the museum's outreach work with schools.
examples.zh: 回答「你为什么想在这里工作」时，我提到了博物馆面向学校的推广活动。

examples.en: When asked "Why do you want to work here?", I mentioned a community program I had visited.
examples.zh: 听到「你为什么想在这里工作」时，我提到了自己参观过的社区项目。

collocations: answer "Why do you want to work here?"
prepare for "Why do you want to work here?"
a response to "Why do you want to work here?"

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify their strong abilities or qualities

examples.en: For "What are your strengths?" I picked one skill I had used in two roles.
examples.zh: 回答「你有哪些优势」时，我选了一项在两个岗位上都用过的技能。

examples.en: I practiced answering "What are your strengths?" with a story about organizing our exhibition.
examples.zh: 我练习用筹办展览的经历回答「你有哪些优势」。

collocations: answer "What are your strengths?" with an example

words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to identify their biggest area for improvement

examples.en: When I heard "What is your greatest weakness?", I talked about learning to delegate tasks.
examples.zh: 听到「你最大的不足是什么」时，我谈了自己如何学习把任务交给别人。

examples.en: I practiced answering "What is your greatest weakness?" with an example of something I was improving.
examples.zh: 我用一件自己正在改进的事练习回答「你最大的不足是什么」。

collocations: practice answering "What is your greatest weakness?"
a response to "What is your greatest weakness?"

words.expression: where do you see yourself in five years
words.lemma: where do you see yourself in five years
words.zhGloss: 五年后有什么职业规划
words.enDefinition: A question about someone's plans or career expectations several years ahead
acceptedZhAnswers: 五年后有什么职业规划
acceptedEnVariants: where do you see yourself in five years

examples.en: When asked "Where do you see yourself in five years?", I explained which skills I hoped to develop.
examples.zh: 听到「五年后有什么职业规划」时，我说了自己希望培养哪些技能。

examples.en: I answered "Where do you see yourself in five years?" by describing the work I wanted.
examples.zh: 我用自己想做什么样的工作回答了「五年后有什么职业规划」。

collocations: ask "Where do you see yourself in five years?"
answer "Where do you see yourself in five years?"
prepare for "Where do you see yourself in five years?"

words.enDefinition: A question asking what gives someone energy or purpose at work

examples.en: I talked about helping others when the interviewer asked "What motivates you?"
examples.zh: 被问到「什么让你有工作动力」时，我谈到了帮别人解决小问题。

examples.en: My answer to "What motivates you?" came from a project I had enjoyed at university.
examples.zh: 我用大学里一个自己喜欢的项目来回答「什么让你有工作动力」。

collocations: prepare a response to "What motivates you?"

words.expression: tell me about a time when
words.lemma: tell me about a time when
words.enDefinition: A lead-in requesting an example of something someone did before
acceptedEnVariants: tell me about a time when

examples.en: The interviewer began with "Tell me about a time when" and asked about missing a deadline.
examples.zh: 面试官以「请讲一次你曾……的经历」开头，问起没赶上截止日期的情况。

examples.en: I recognized "Tell me about a time when" as a prompt for a specific example from the past.
examples.zh: 我知道「请讲一次你曾……的经历」是在让人举出一个过去的具体例子。

collocations: tell me about a time when you led a team
tell me about a time when you made a mistake
tell me about a time when you had to ask for help

words.expression: describe a time when you worked under pressure
words.lemma: describe a time when you worked under pressure
words.zhGloss: 请描述一次在压力下工作
words.enDefinition: A prompt asking for an example of working in demanding circumstances
acceptedZhAnswers: 请描述一次在压力下工作
acceptedEnVariants: describe a time when you worked under pressure

examples.en: The prompt was "Describe a time when you worked under pressure." I described exam week.
examples.zh: 练习题是「请描述一次在压力下工作的经历」，我选了考试周的一件事。

examples.en: I answered "Describe a time when you worked under pressure" with my experience opening the shop alone.
examples.zh: 我用独自开店的经历回答了「请描述一次在压力下工作的经历」。

collocations: ask "Describe a time when you worked under pressure."
prepare an example for "Describe a time when you worked under pressure."
a response to "Describe a time when you worked under pressure."

words.expression: how do you handle competing priorities
words.lemma: how do you handle competing priorities
words.enDefinition: A question about deciding what to do when tasks conflict
acceptedEnVariants: how do you handle competing priorities

examples.en: I heard "How do you handle competing priorities?" and talked about two deadlines in the same week.
examples.zh: 听到「如何取舍不同的任务」时，我谈到了同一周的两个截止日期。

examples.en: A sample question asked "How do you handle competing priorities?" after listing two urgent requests from supervisors.
examples.zh: 一道样题列出两位主管提出的紧急请求后问「如何取舍不同的任务」。

collocations: answer "How do you handle competing priorities?"
practice answering "How do you handle competing priorities?"
prepare for "How do you handle competing priorities?"

words.expression: what did you learn from that experience
words.lemma: what did you learn from that experience
words.zhGloss: 那段经历让你学到什么
words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to reflect on lessons from past events
acceptedZhAnswers: 那段经历让你学到什么
acceptedEnVariants: what did you learn from that experience

examples.en: After I explained the delay, the interviewer asked "What did you learn from that experience?" and waited.
examples.zh: 我说明延误的原因后，面试官问「那段经历让你学到了什么」，然后等我回答。

examples.en: I explained a communication lesson when asked "What did you learn from that experience?"
examples.zh: 模拟面试时，我用一条沟通方面的经验回答「那段经历让你学到了什么」。

collocations: ask "What did you learn from that experience?"
answer "What did you learn from that experience?"
follow up with "What did you learn from that experience?"

words.enDefinition: A question inviting someone to reconsider an earlier choice or action

examples.en: When she asked "What would you do differently?", I said I would clarify the deadlines first.
examples.zh: 她问「你会换成什么做法」时，我说自己会先确认各个截止时间。

examples.en: The follow-up "What would you do differently?" led us to discuss how I asked for feedback.
examples.zh: 「你会换成什么做法」这个追问让我们谈起我怎样征求反馈。

collocations: ask "What would you do differently next time?"
follow up with "What would you do differently?"

words.expression: do you have any questions for us
words.lemma: do you have any questions for us
words.enDefinition: An invitation for the candidate to ask the interviewers questions
acceptedEnVariants: do you have any questions for us

examples.en: I asked about training when the panel said "Do you have any questions for us?" at the end.
examples.zh: 面试快结束时，小组问「你有什么想问我们的」，我就询问了培训情况。

examples.en: The panel asked "Do you have any questions for us?" I asked about supervision.
examples.zh: 模拟面试最后问「你有什么想问我们的」，我趁机了解了指导安排。

collocations: end with "Do you have any questions for us?"
answer "Do you have any questions for us?"
prepare for "Do you have any questions for us?"

words.enDefinition: Abilities or qualities someone applies effectively in a work setting

examples.en: I talked about my professional strengths using examples from the library and the lab.
examples.zh: 我用在图书馆和实验室的例子来谈自己的「职业优势」。

examples.en: My adviser asked which of my professional strengths mattered most for this role.
examples.zh: 顾问问我有哪些「职业优势」对这份工作最重要。

words.enDefinition: A skill or aspect of performance that someone could develop further

examples.en: I named delegation as an area for improvement and explained what I had changed.
examples.zh: 我说分派任务这方面「有待改进」，并解释了自己作了哪些改变。

examples.en: The feedback identified my pacing as an area for improvement for the next interview.
examples.zh: 反馈指出，我的语速是下次面试时「有待改进之处」。

collocations: an area for improvement in communication

words.enDefinition: The kinds of work or achievements someone hopes for long term

examples.en: My career aspirations changed after I worked on a student outreach project.
examples.zh: 参加学生推广项目之后，我的「职业抱负」变了。

examples.en: The interview gave me a chance to explain my career aspirations in education.
examples.zh: 面试给了我机会说明自己在教育领域的「职业抱负」。

words.enDefinition: The personal reason someone decided to apply for a role

examples.en: I explained my motivation for applying by talking about the museum's community work.
examples.zh: 我谈到博物馆的社区工作，借此说明了自己的「应聘动机」。

examples.en: The panel asked about my motivation for applying before discussing my class projects.
examples.zh: 面试小组先询问我的「应聘动机」，然后才谈课程项目。

words.enDefinition: The way someone generally organizes and carries out their work

examples.en: I used my campus job to illustrate my working style during busy weeks.
examples.zh: 我用校内工作举例，说明自己在繁忙时的「工作方式」。

examples.en: The panel asked how my working style changed when I worked with others.
examples.zh: 面试小组问我，与人合作时自己的「工作方式」有什么变化。

words.enDefinition: The ways team members interact, communicate, and influence one another

examples.en: The example showed how two new members changed our team dynamics that semester.
examples.zh: 这个例子说明，那学期两名新成员如何改变了我们的「团队互动模式」。

examples.en: I asked about team dynamics after hearing how the team divided its work.
examples.zh: 听完团队的分工介绍后，我问了他们的「团队互动模式」。

words.enDefinition: A person's usual method for identifying and addressing a difficulty

examples.en: The interviewer asked how my approach to problem-solving changed when information was missing.
examples.zh: 面试官问我，在信息不足时，「解决问题的方法」会怎样调整。

examples.en: My approach to problem-solving involved checking what the users needed before changing anything.
examples.zh: 我「解决问题的方法」是先确认用户的需求，再作改动。

words.enDefinition: Important tasks competing for the same limited time or resources

examples.en: I used a campus project to explain how I managed conflicting priorities.
examples.zh: 我用一个校内项目来说明自己如何处理「互相冲突的优先事项」。

examples.en: The question about conflicting priorities involved deadlines from two different departments.
examples.zh: 有关「互相冲突的优先事项」的题目涉及两个不同院系的截止时间。

words.enDefinition: To finish work on time despite having little time to complete it

examples.en: I described how our team divided tasks to meet a tight deadline before orientation.
examples.zh: 我描述了迎新前团队如何分工，最终「赶上紧迫的截止期限」。

examples.en: The interviewer asked how I checked my work while trying to meet a tight deadline.
examples.zh: 面试官问我，努力「赶上紧迫的截止期限」时是怎样检查工作的。

collocations: work together to meet a tight deadline
manage to meet a tight deadline

words.enDefinition: To respond constructively when people do not share an opinion

examples.en: I described how I had to handle a disagreement between two club members.
examples.zh: 我讲了自己不得不「处理意见分歧」的一次经历，意见不合的是两位社团成员。

examples.en: The adviser asked how I would handle a disagreement on a small team.
examples.zh: 顾问问我在小团队里会怎样「处理意见分歧」。

collocations: handle a disagreement with a teammate

words.enDefinition: To respond to difficulties that delay or disrupt progress

examples.en: The panel asked how I had learned to deal with setbacks at university.
examples.zh: 小组问我在大学里是怎样学会「应对挫折」的。

examples.en: I used the canceled exhibition to explain how I deal with setbacks without losing momentum.
examples.zh: 我以展览取消为例，说明自己如何「应对挫折」并保持工作进度。

words.enDefinition: To start doing something without waiting to be asked

examples.en: I gave an example of when I had to take the initiative without a supervisor nearby.
examples.zh: 我举了个例子，说明没有主管在场时，我怎样「主动采取行动」。

examples.en: My adviser wanted to know what made me take the initiative on the project.
examples.zh: 顾问想知道是什么促使我在项目中「主动采取行动」。

collocations: take the initiative on a project

words.enDefinition: To adjust how you act when conditions become different

examples.en: I talked about learning to adapt to change when our supervisor left midsemester.
examples.zh: 我谈到了主管在学期中途离开后，自己如何学着「适应变化」。

examples.en: The panel asked how I would adapt to change during a busy term.
examples.zh: 面试小组问我在繁忙的学期里会怎样「适应变化」。

words.enDefinition: A technique that structures examples around situation, task, action, and result

examples.en: I used the STAR method to order my story about a busy shift.
examples.zh: 我用「情境任务行动结果法」理顺了自己在忙碌班次中的经历。

examples.en: The STAR method helped me explain what changed after we made the decision.
examples.zh: 「情境任务行动结果法」帮我说清团队作出决定后发生了什么变化。

collocations: an example using the STAR method

words.enDefinition: To give enough background for someone to understand what follows

examples.en: I used two sentences to set the scene before explaining what I changed.
examples.zh: 我先用两句话「交代背景」，再解释自己作了哪些改变。

examples.en: My adviser asked me to set the scene by naming the project and team.
examples.zh: 顾问让我先说项目和团队的名字，以此「交代背景」。

collocations: set the scene for a story
use one sentence to set the scene

words.enDefinition: To add information that helps someone understand a topic or experience

examples.en: I mentioned when the internship started to give some context for my example.
examples.zh: 我提到实习开始的时间，为自己的例子「提供一些背景」。

examples.en: The panel asked me to give some context before discussing the change in attendance.
examples.zh: 面试小组请我先「提供一些背景」，再谈出席人数的变化。

collocations: give some context for the decision

words.enDefinition: To briefly state the work that needed to be done

examples.en: I used one sentence to outline the task before explaining my choice of tool.
examples.zh: 我用一句话「概述任务」，再解释为什么选了那个工具。

examples.en: The adviser asked me to outline the task without listing every small detail.
examples.zh: 顾问让我「概述任务」，用不着列出每个小细节。

collocations: outline the task for the team

words.enDefinition: To say why you reached a particular judgment or decision

examples.en: The sample prompt asks you to explain your reasoning for changing the meeting time.
examples.zh: 样题让你「解释你的理由」，说明为什么调整开会时间。

examples.en: It is easier to explain your reasoning when you remember what choices were available.
examples.zh: 如果记得当时有哪些选项，就更容易「解释你的理由」。

collocations: explain your reasoning for a decision
invite someone to explain their reasoning

words.enDefinition: The things you personally did in a particular situation

examples.en: The practice guide says to focus on the actions you took to solve the problem.
examples.zh: 练习指南说，要着重讲「你采取的行动」怎样解决了问题。

examples.en: The interviewer asked how the actions you took affected the rest of the team.
examples.zh: 面试官问「你采取的行动」对其他队员有什么影响。

collocations: focus on the actions you took

words.enDefinition: To describe what happened as a result of an action

examples.en: I used the attendance figures to explain the outcome of our scheduling changes.
examples.zh: 我用出席人数的数据来「解释结果」，说明调整日程有什么效果。

examples.en: The adviser gave me a second chance to explain the outcome of the project.
examples.zh: 顾问又给了我一次机会，让我「解释结果」，说明这个项目最后怎么样了。

collocations: explain the outcome of a decision
explain the outcome to the panel

words.enDefinition: To draw attention to the main differences after something happened

examples.en: I compared two weeks of waiting times to highlight what changed at our desk.
examples.zh: 我比较了服务台两周的等候时间，以「着重说明有哪些变化」。

examples.en: The practice guide asked me to highlight what changed after we rewrote the instructions.
examples.zh: 练习指南让我「着重说明有哪些变化」，指我们重写操作说明之后的变化。

collocations: highlight what changed after the decision
highlight what changed in the process

words.enDefinition: Something understood as a result of a previous experience

examples.en: My answer ended with one lesson learned from the canceled event.
examples.zh: 我在回答的最后说了一条活动取消后总结出的「经验教训」。

examples.en: The interviewer asked whether the lesson learned affected how I planned later events.
examples.zh: 面试官问，这条「经验教训」是否影响了后来我策划活动的方式。

words.enDefinition: To think carefully about a past event and what it taught you

examples.en: The interviewer asked me to reflect on an experience where I changed my mind.
examples.zh: 面试官让我「反思一段经历」，就是我曾改变主意的那一次。

examples.en: I used the practice session to reflect on an experience from my summer placement.
examples.zh: 我利用模拟面试「反思一段经历」，来自自己的暑期实习。

collocations: reflect on an experience at work
take time to reflect on an experience
reflect on an experience from university

words.enDefinition: To demonstrate the knowledge or understanding gained from an experience

examples.en: One good way to show what you learned is to describe a later decision.
examples.zh: 要「展示你学到了什么」，一个好办法是描述之后作出的一项决定。

examples.en: The question gave you a chance to show what you learned from the first project.
examples.zh: 这道题给你机会「展示你学到了什么」，尤其是从第一个项目中。

collocations: show what you learned from a setback
show what you learned through an example
explain how to show what you learned

words.enDefinition: To select a particular event that relates directly to the topic

examples.en: I took a moment to choose a relevant example before answering the question about teamwork.
examples.zh: 回答团队合作的问题前，我花了点时间「选择相关例子」。

examples.en: The worksheet helped me choose a relevant example from three different jobs I had held.
examples.zh: 这张练习表帮我「选择相关例子」，有三份做过的工作可供选择。

collocations: choose a relevant example from your experience
choose a relevant example for each question
take time to choose a relevant example

words.expression: link your experience to the role
words.lemma: link your experience to the role
words.zhGloss: 把经历与岗位联系起来
words.enDefinition: To explain how your past activities relate to the job
acceptedZhAnswers: 把经历与岗位联系起来
acceptedEnVariants: link your experience to the role

examples.en: The adviser asked you to link your experience to the role using one example from university.
examples.zh: 顾问让你用一个大学里的例子「把经历与岗位联系起来」。

examples.en: The opening question gives you a chance to link your experience to the role right away.
examples.zh: 开场问题让你有机会一开始就「把经历与岗位联系起来」。

collocations: link your experience to the role clearly
help link your experience to the role
learn to link your experience to the role

words.enDefinition: To draw attention to something someone does particularly well

examples.en: I used my first campus job to highlight a strength in dealing with visitors.
examples.zh: 我用第一份校内工作来「突出一项优势」，就是擅长和来访者打交道。

examples.en: The adviser asked me to highlight a strength that mattered for this particular job.
examples.zh: 顾问让我「突出一项优势」，这项优势得对这份工作有帮助。

collocations: highlight a strength in an answer
highlight a strength the role requires
use a story to highlight a strength

words.enDefinition: To openly say that you did something wrong or incorrectly

examples.en: My story explained why I chose to acknowledge a mistake during the team meeting.
examples.zh: 我的经历说明了为什么我选择在团队会议上「承认错误」。

examples.en: The practice question asked how I would acknowledge a mistake without blaming a colleague.
examples.zh: 练习题问我会如何「承认错误」，同时避免责怪同事。

collocations: be willing to acknowledge a mistake
acknowledge a mistake in an answer

words.enDefinition: To accept accountability for an action, decision, or outcome

examples.en: I described how I chose to take responsibility for sending the wrong file.
examples.zh: 我讲了自己如何选择「承担责任」，为发错文件这件事负责。

examples.en: The interviewer asked when I had learned to take responsibility without being asked.
examples.zh: 面试官问我什么时候学会了主动「承担责任」。

words.enDefinition: To request someone's comments on how something went or could improve

examples.en: I learned to ask for feedback after meetings rather than guessing what people thought.
examples.zh: 我学会了在会后「征求反馈」，而不是猜测别人的想法。

examples.en: My example explained why I chose to ask for feedback halfway through the project.
examples.zh: 我举例说明了为什么选择在项目进行到一半时「征求反馈」。

collocations: ask for feedback on an answer
ask for feedback from a supervisor

words.enDefinition: To use others' comments to make changes or improvements

examples.en: I described how I learned to act on feedback after my first week at work.
examples.zh: 我描述了自己在上班第一周过后怎样学着「根据反馈作改进」。

examples.en: The panel asked how I would act on feedback that I disagreed with.
examples.zh: 面试小组问我，遇到不赞同的反馈会怎样「根据反馈作改进」。

collocations: act on feedback from a supervisor

words.enDefinition: To mention a worry about a potential difficulty or problem

examples.en: I explained why I chose to raise a concern before we changed the schedule.
examples.zh: 我解释了为什么在调整日程之前选择「提出顾虑」。

examples.en: The interviewer asked how I would raise a concern in front of a busy team.
examples.zh: 面试官问我，面对正忙着的团队，我会怎样「提出顾虑」。

collocations: raise a concern with a supervisor

words.enDefinition: To agree on a solution after each side gives something up

examples.en: I described how we managed to reach a compromise about the club's budget.
examples.zh: 我讲了大家是怎样在社团预算上「达成妥协」的。

examples.en: My answer explained how I helped two classmates reach a compromise during the project.
examples.zh: 我在回答中解释了项目期间怎样帮助两位同学「达成妥协」。

collocations: reach a compromise with a colleague
work together to reach a compromise

words.enDefinition: To decide which things need attention before others

examples.en: I described how I prioritize tasks when two events started at once.
examples.zh: 我描述了两场活动同时开始时，自己怎样「给任务排优先级」。

examples.en: The interviewer asked how I learned to prioritize tasks at the service desk.
examples.zh: 面试官问我是在服务台怎样学会「给任务排优先级」的。

words.enDefinition: To change the way you do something as circumstances develop

examples.en: In this example, you need to adjust your approach when the team size changes.
examples.zh: 在这个例子里，团队人数变化时，你需要「调整自己的做法」。

examples.en: The sample prompt asks how you would adjust your approach after negative feedback.
examples.zh: 样题问你收到负面反馈后会怎样「调整自己的做法」。

collocations: adjust your approach to a problem
be ready to adjust your approach

words.enDefinition: To improve your understanding or behavior after doing something wrong

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to explain how we might learn from a mistake at work.
examples.zh: 导师让我们说说工作中可以怎样「从错误中吸取教训」。

examples.en: The interviewer wanted to know how I had managed to learn from a mistake.
examples.zh: 面试官想了解我是怎样「从错误中吸取教训」的。

collocations: learn from a mistake at work
help someone learn from a mistake
be willing to learn from a mistake

words.enDefinition: To do useful work outside the tasks someone has given you

examples.en: The question asked when you chose to go beyond your assigned duties to help a team.
examples.zh: 题目问你什么时候选择「做超出分内职责的事」来帮助团队。

examples.en: Our adviser asked for an example of when you go beyond your assigned duties at work.
examples.zh: 顾问让你举个在工作中「做超出分内职责的事」的例子。

collocations: go beyond your assigned duties to help
choose to go beyond your assigned duties
learn when to go beyond your assigned duties

words.enDefinition: To respond practically when something challenging or uncomfortable happens

examples.en: I used my café job to show how I handle a difficult situation with customers.
examples.zh: 我用咖啡馆工作的经历说明，与顾客打交道时自己如何「处理棘手情况」。

examples.en: The practice panel asked how I would handle a difficult situation during my first week.
examples.zh: 模拟面试小组问我，第一周遇到问题时会怎样「处理棘手情况」。

collocations: learn to handle a difficult situation
handle a difficult situation at work

words.enDefinition: A response that states the main point in few words

examples.en: I gave a concise answer about my coursework before moving to my project.
examples.zh: 我对课程作了「简明回答」，然后谈到自己的项目。

examples.en: The adviser helped me turn a long explanation into a concise answer.
examples.zh: 顾问帮我把一段冗长的解释改成了「简明回答」。

words.enDefinition: A response with a logical order that listeners can follow

examples.en: A well-structured answer helped the panel see how each step led to the result.
examples.zh: 「条理清楚的回答」让面试小组明白了各个步骤怎么带来结果。

examples.en: I practiced turning my scattered notes into a well-structured answer about teamwork.
examples.zh: 我练习把零散的笔记整理成「条理清楚的回答」，用于团队合作的话题。

collocations: a well-structured answer to a question

words.enDefinition: A response prepared or given during rehearsal for a real interview

examples.en: I recorded a practice answer to hear where I spoke too quickly.
examples.zh: 我录下「练习用的回答」，听听自己哪些地方说得太快。

examples.en: The adviser asked me to shorten the opening of my practice answer.
examples.zh: 顾问让我缩短「练习用的回答」的开头。

words.enDefinition: A fixed response someone has learned to repeat from memory

examples.en: My tutor noticed that my memorized answer did not address the question.
examples.zh: 导师注意到我「背熟的回答」没有答到题目上。

examples.en: I changed one example because the memorized answer sounded unnatural when spoken.
examples.zh: 「背熟的回答」说出来不自然，所以我换了一个例子。

words.enDefinition: To respond using language you choose instead of repeating a script

examples.en: The practice sheet encourages you to answer in your own words after reading the prompt.
examples.zh: 练习单鼓励你读完题目后「用自己的话回答」。

examples.en: You can answer in your own words even when you have rehearsed the story before.
examples.zh: 即使之前练习过这段经历，你也可以「用自己的话回答」。

collocations: try to answer in your own words
feel free to answer in your own words
take time to answer in your own words

words.enDefinition: To state what matters immediately without unnecessary introduction

examples.en: The adviser told me to get straight to the point when explaining why I applied.
examples.zh: 顾问让我解释为什么应聘时要「开门见山」。

examples.en: I cut the first two sentences so I could get straight to the point more quickly.
examples.zh: 我删掉了前两句，好更快「开门见山」。

collocations: try to get straight to the point
get straight to the point in your answer
help someone get straight to the point

words.enDefinition: To keep a response focused on what was actually asked

examples.en: I used the prompt on my notes to stick to the question during practice.
examples.zh: 练习时，我看着笔记上的题目，提醒自己「紧扣问题」。

examples.en: The adviser asked me to stick to the question when talking about the launch.
examples.zh: 顾问让我谈到发布活动时「紧扣问题」。

collocations: try to stick to the question
remember to stick to the question

words.enDefinition: To stop remembering what you were about to say

examples.en: It is easy to lose your train of thought when someone interrupts halfway through a story.
examples.zh: 有人讲到一半被打断时，很容易「思路突然中断」。

examples.en: My coach explained what to do if you lose your train of thought in an interview.
examples.zh: 教练介绍了面试中「思路突然中断」时可以怎么应对。

collocations: momentarily lose your train of thought
lose your train of thought mid-sentence
worry you might lose your train of thought

words.enDefinition: To pause briefly before deciding what to say or do

examples.en: The panel said I could take a moment to think before answering the last question.
examples.zh: 小组说回答最后一道题之前，我可以「先想一下」。

examples.en: I learned to take a moment to think when the wording of a question surprised me.
examples.zh: 遇到出乎意料的提问时，我学会了「先想一下」。

collocations: feel free to take a moment to think
take a moment to think before speaking
take a moment to think before you answer

words.enDefinition: To wait briefly before beginning a response to a question

examples.en: I practiced how to pause before answering rather than filling the silence with words.
examples.zh: 我练习怎样「回答前停顿一下」，不要为了填补空白就随口说话。

examples.en: The interviewer told our group it was fine to pause before answering.
examples.zh: 面试官告诉我们小组，「回答前停顿一下」也没关系。

collocations: pause before answering a difficult question

words.enDefinition: A polite request to hear the same question again

examples.en: I asked "Could you repeat the question?" after the noise outside covered the last few words.
examples.zh: 外面的噪声盖过了最后几个词，我问「您能重复一下问题吗」。

examples.en: We practiced saying "Could you repeat the question?" without starting to answer a different question.
examples.zh: 我们练习说「您能重复一下问题吗」，避免听岔了就答成另一个问题。

collocations: could you repeat the question, please?
sorry, could you repeat the question?
could you repeat the question one more time?

words.enDefinition: A polite request to hear a question expressed another way

examples.en: When the wording confused me, I asked "Could you rephrase the question?" and waited for the reply.
examples.zh: 没理解提问的措辞时，我问「您能换个说法提问吗」，然后等对方回应。

examples.en: My tutor suggested "Could you rephrase the question?" when a question uses an unfamiliar term.
examples.zh: 导师建议，题目中有不熟悉的术语时，可以问「您能换个说法提问吗」。

collocations: could you rephrase the question, please?
sorry, could you rephrase the question?
could you rephrase the question for me?

words.enDefinition: A polite lead-in for checking your interpretation of something heard

examples.en: I said "If I understand correctly, you want an example from work." My partner nodded.
examples.zh: 练习时我说，「如果我理解得没错」，您希望我举一个工作中的例子。

examples.en: The candidate began with "If I understand correctly" before checking which role we meant.
examples.zh: 应聘者先说「如果我理解得没错」，然后确认我们指的是哪个岗位。

collocations: if I understand correctly, you are asking about timing
if I understand correctly, you mean the second project
begin with if I understand correctly

words.enDefinition: A polite request for short thinking time before responding

examples.en: When the final question surprised me, I asked "May I take a moment?" before responding.
examples.zh: 最后一道题让我有些意外，我在回答之前问「我可以先想一下吗」。

examples.en: Our adviser suggested "May I take a moment?" for questions that need some thought.
examples.zh: 顾问建议，遇到需要想一想的问题时可以说「我可以先想一下吗」。

collocations: may I take a moment to think
may I take a moment to consider that
may I take a moment before answering

words.expression: let me give you an example
words.lemma: let me give you an example
words.enDefinition: A phrase introducing a specific instance to explain a point
acceptedEnVariants: let me give you an example

examples.en: I said "Let me give you an example" before describing a busy afternoon at the desk.
examples.zh: 我先说「我来给您举个例子」，然后讲了服务台一个忙碌的下午。

examples.en: The student used "Let me give you an example" to introduce a story about their project.
examples.zh: 这位学生用「我来给您举个例子」引出自己的项目经历。

collocations: let me give you an example from work
let me give you an example of what I mean
let me give you an example from last term

words.enDefinition: Words used to introduce a clearer explanation of a point

examples.en: I said "What I mean is" before explaining exactly how we shared the work.
examples.zh: 我先说「我的意思是」，然后具体解释我们怎样分工。

examples.en: The coach noticed I kept saying "What I mean is" even when my meaning was clear.
examples.zh: 教练发现即使我已经说得很清楚，也还在反复说「我的意思是」。

collocations: what I mean is that the deadline changed
what I mean is that we shared the work
what I mean is, I handled the records

words.enDefinition: A phrase introducing how someone would respond in an imagined situation

examples.en: I began "In that situation I would" when the panel asked about an unfamiliar scenario.
examples.zh: 小组问起不熟悉的情境时，我以「在那种情况下我会」开头。

examples.en: We practiced completing "In that situation I would" with one clear and realistic action.
examples.zh: 我们练习在「在那种情况下我会」后面接一个明确而可行的行动。

collocations: in that situation I would check the deadline
in that situation I would speak to my supervisor
in that situation I would ask for more details

words.enDefinition: Words that introduce context before someone describes the main point

examples.en: I said "To give you some background" before explaining why the student group needed help.
examples.zh: 我先说「先介绍一下背景」，再解释为什么这个学生小组需要帮助。

examples.en: The tutor shortened the part that followed "To give you some background" in my practice answer.
examples.zh: 导师缩短了我练习回答中「先介绍一下背景」后面的内容。

collocations: to give you some background on the project
to give you some background on the team
to give you some background, we had two shifts

words.enDefinition: An expression used to introduce the first point or example

examples.en: My answer began with "Let me start with" before I introduced our library project.
examples.zh: 我的回答先说「我先从……说起」，随后介绍了图书馆项目。

examples.en: I practiced following "Let me start with" with a brief description of my role.
examples.zh: 我练习在「我先从……说起」之后简要描述自己的角色。

collocations: let me start with a recent example
let me start with my role
let me start with the result

words.enDefinition: A phrase introducing the most important lesson from an experience

examples.en: I used "The main takeaway was" to finish my answer about a mistake.
examples.zh: 我用「我最大的收获是」来收尾，回答的是我曾犯过的一个错误。

examples.en: The tutor asked me to complete "The main takeaway was" with one lesson I could explain.
examples.zh: 导师让我在「我最大的收获是」后面接一条我能解释清楚的经验。

collocations: the main takeaway was the need for clearer roles
the main takeaway was that planning helped
the main takeaway was about communication

words.expression: thanks for taking the time to meet with me
words.lemma: thanks for taking the time to meet with me
words.zhGloss: 谢谢您抽时间与我见面
words.enDefinition: A polite expression of appreciation at the end of a meeting
acceptedZhAnswers: 谢谢您抽时间与我见面
acceptedEnVariants: thanks for taking the time to meet with me

examples.en: I closed with "Thanks for taking the time to meet with me" before gathering my notes.
examples.zh: 我最后说「谢谢您抽时间与我见面」，然后收好了笔记。

examples.en: I practiced saying "Thanks for taking the time to meet with me" as I left the room.
examples.zh: 我练习离开房间时说「谢谢您抽时间与我见面」。

collocations: thanks for taking the time to meet with me today
thanks for taking the time to meet with me in person
and thanks for taking the time to meet with me this morning

words.enDefinition: Information communicated through posture, gestures, or facial expressions

examples.en: The practice video helped me notice my body language while I listened.
examples.zh: 练习录像让我留意到自己在倾听时的「肢体语言」。

examples.en: We discussed how body language can change a listener's impression of an answer.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「肢体语言」怎样改变听者对回答的印象。

words.enDefinition: To look at someone's eyes while speaking or listening

examples.en: I tried to make eye contact with the person who asked the question.
examples.zh: 我试着和提问者「进行眼神交流」。

examples.en: The video showed when I tended to make eye contact during my answers.
examples.zh: 视频让我看到自己回答时通常什么时候会「进行眼神交流」。

collocations: make eye contact with the interviewer

words.enDefinition: The speed at which a person speaks during a conversation

examples.en: My speaking pace picked up when I reached the end of the story.
examples.zh: 我讲到故事快结束时，「说话速度」加快了。

examples.en: The practice helped me find a speaking pace that still sounded natural.
examples.zh: 练习帮我找到一种听起来仍然自然的「说话速度」。

words.enDefinition: The quality of someone's voice that conveys an attitude or feeling

examples.en: The coach noticed my tone of voice became softer when I explained the mistake.
examples.zh: 教练注意到我解释那次错误时，「说话语气」变柔和了。

examples.en: My roommate said the same words sounded different in another tone of voice.
examples.zh: 室友说，同样的话换一种「说话语气」就会听起来不一样。

words.enDefinition: Careful attention to a speaker combined with responses showing understanding

examples.en: The group exercise showed how active listening helped us notice overlapping ideas.
examples.zh: 小组练习展示了「积极倾听」怎样帮助我们发现彼此观点中的共同点。

examples.en: The adviser discussed active listening before we tried a paired interview exercise.
examples.zh: 我们两人一组练习面试之前，顾问先讲了「积极倾听」。

collocations: use active listening in a discussion

words.enDefinition: To notice a signal suggesting what someone wants or means

examples.en: I learned to pick up on a cue that the panel wanted a shorter answer.
examples.zh: 我学会了「察觉到提示」，明白面试小组希望回答简短一点。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how to pick up on a cue without interrupting the person speaking.
examples.zh: 导师示范了怎样在不打断讲话者的情况下「察觉到提示」。

collocations: pick up on a cue from the interviewer
quickly pick up on a cue
learn to pick up on a cue

words.enDefinition: To express the same response in a different and clearer way

examples.en: The tutor asked me to rephrase an answer that was difficult to follow.
examples.zh: 导师让我把一段不容易听懂的答案「换个说法重述」。

examples.en: I practiced how to rephrase an answer without changing any of the facts.
examples.zh: 我练习怎样在保留原有事实的情况下「换个说法重述答案」。

collocations: ask someone to rephrase an answer
rephrase an answer in simpler language

words.enDefinition: To express the central idea you want someone to remember

examples.en: The handout says to state your main point before giving details about your example.
examples.zh: 讲义说应先「说清你的重点」，然后再讲例子细节。

examples.en: I asked my partner whether it helped to state your main point earlier.
examples.zh: 我问搭档，提前「说清重点」有没有帮助。

collocations: state your main point in one sentence

words.enDefinition: To bring your reply to a brief and natural conclusion

examples.en: The tutor showed how to wrap up your answer without repeating the whole story.
examples.zh: 导师示范了怎样「结束回答」，用不着把整个故事再讲一遍。

examples.en: The guide suggests using one brief sentence to wrap up your answer.
examples.zh: 指南建议用一句简短的话「结束你的回答」。

collocations: wrap up your answer with the result
learn to wrap up your answer

words.enDefinition: To become calm again after feeling upset or nervous

examples.en: A short pause can help you recover your composure after an unexpected question.
examples.zh: 遇到出乎意料的问题时，短暂停顿能帮助你「恢复镇定」。

examples.en: My tutor showed me how to recover your composure without rushing the next sentence.
examples.zh: 导师教我怎样「恢复镇定」，不用急着说下一句。

collocations: take time to recover your composure

words.enDefinition: Anxiety or nervous feelings before or during a job interview

examples.en: A short walk helped me manage my interview nerves before the appointment.
examples.zh: 面试前散了一小会儿步，我的「面试紧张情绪」缓和了些。

examples.en: The first question was straightforward, and my interview nerves soon eased.
examples.zh: 第一个问题很直接，我的「面试紧张情绪」很快就缓解了。

words.enDefinition: To keep the way you speak suitable for a formal interaction

examples.en: The coach showed how to maintain a professional tone while explaining a disagreement at work.
examples.zh: 教练示范了怎么在解释工作中的分歧时「保持专业语气」。

examples.en: We practiced how to maintain a professional tone when our partners asked difficult questions.
examples.zh: 搭档提出难题时，我们练习怎样「保持专业语气」。

collocations: maintain a professional tone when disagreeing

words.enDefinition: The interview following an employer's first interview in the same process

examples.en: My second-round interview included questions about decisions I made during my placement.
examples.zh: 我的「第二轮面试」问到了一些我在实习时作过的决定。

examples.en: The second-round interview focused more on teamwork than my first meeting did.
examples.zh: 相比第一次面谈，「第二轮面试」更关注团队合作。

words.enDefinition: A discussion reviewing what happened during a job interview

examples.en: During our interview debrief, I wrote down two questions that surprised me.
examples.zh: 我们做「面试复盘」时，我记下了两道出乎意料的问题。

examples.en: My interview debrief focused on which examples were easiest to explain clearly.
examples.zh: 我的「面试复盘」主要谈了哪些经历最容易讲清楚。

collocations: an interview debrief with an adviser

words.enDefinition: A specific event or experience that illustrates a relevant work ability

examples.en: The first question gave me time to share a job-related example from the café.
examples.zh: 第一道题让我有机会分享一个在咖啡馆工作时「与岗位相关的实例」。

examples.en: I used a job-related example to show how I handled an unexpected delay.
examples.zh: 我用一个「与岗位相关的实例」说明自己怎样处理突发延误。

words.enDefinition: To practice saying a response before the real conversation

examples.en: I used a voice recorder to rehearse an answer about my summer placement.
examples.zh: 我借助录音设备「预先练习回答」，话题是我的暑期实习。

examples.en: We took turns so each of us could rehearse an answer and get feedback.
examples.zh: 我们轮流来，每个人都可以「预先练习回答」，再听听反馈。

collocations: rehearse an answer with a friend
rehearse an answer before an interview

words.enDefinition: To create a friendly connection based on mutual understanding

examples.en: I found it easier to build rapport after we discussed the campus café.
examples.zh: 我们聊过校园咖啡馆之后，我觉得比较容易「建立融洽关系」。

examples.en: The adviser showed how a genuine question can help build rapport.
examples.zh: 顾问示范了一个真诚的问题能怎样帮助双方「建立融洽关系」。

words.enDefinition: To finish a conversation leaving people with a good feeling

examples.en: I thanked the panel for their questions to end on a positive note.
examples.zh: 我感谢了面试小组的提问，让谈话「以积极的话收尾」。

examples.en: The adviser let me practice how to end on a positive note after a difficult interview.
examples.zh: 顾问让我练习在一场不太顺利的面试中，怎样「以积极的话收尾」。

collocations: end on a positive note after a difficult question
try to end on a positive note
help an interview end on a positive note

words.enDefinition: To remember a particular event rather than a general pattern

examples.en: I checked my placement notes to recall a specific incident involving a late delivery.
examples.zh: 我翻看实习笔记，想「回想一件具体的事」，和一次交货延迟有关。

examples.en: The practice question asked you to recall a specific incident from a group project.
examples.zh: 练习题请你「回想一件具体的事」，可以选一个小组项目里的经历。

collocations: try to recall a specific incident
help someone recall a specific incident
recall a specific incident from work

words.enDefinition: To state clearly what made a situation difficult

examples.en: I used the first sentence to identify the challenge before describing what I did.
examples.zh: 我用第一句话「指出遇到的难题」，然后说明自己做了什么。

examples.en: The tutor asked me to identify the challenge without listing every small problem.
examples.zh: 导师让我「指出遇到的难题」，不用把每个小问题都列出来。

collocations: identify the challenge facing the team

words.enDefinition: To tell someone what happened or what a task achieved

examples.en: My tutor reminded me to state the result before ending the story.
examples.zh: 导师提醒我在讲完这段经历之前「说明结果」。

examples.en: I used one figure to state the result of the new booking system.
examples.zh: 我用一个数字「说明结果」，介绍新预订系统的成效。

collocations: state the result in one sentence
state the result before moving on

words.expression: what makes you a good fit for this role
words.lemma: what makes you a good fit for this role
words.zhGloss: 你为什么适合这个岗位
words.enDefinition: A question asking why someone's background matches the role
acceptedZhAnswers: 你为什么适合这个岗位
acceptedEnVariants: what makes you a good fit for this role

examples.en: I heard "What makes you a good fit for this role?" and mentioned my tutoring work.
examples.zh: 听到「你为什么适合这个岗位」，我提到了自己的辅导工作。

examples.en: I answered "What makes you a good fit for this role?" with one clear example.
examples.zh: 我用一个清楚的例子回答「你为什么适合这个岗位」。

collocations: ask "What makes you a good fit for this role?"
a response to "What makes you a good fit for this role?"
prepare for "What makes you a good fit for this role?"

words.enDefinition: A question asking about the action that immediately followed an event

examples.en: The interviewer asked "What did you do next?" after I described the missing files.
examples.zh: 我说完文件丢失的情况后，面试官问「接下来你做了什么」。

examples.en: I heard "What did you do next?" and explained why I spoke to the supervisor.
examples.zh: 听到「接下来你做了什么」，我解释了为什么要去找主管。

collocations: follow up with "What did you do next?"

words.enDefinition: A question asking what evidence showed an effort had worked

examples.en: I gave attendance figures when the manager asked "How did you measure success?" at the interview.
examples.zh: 面试时，经理问「你如何衡量成效」，我就给出了出席人数。

examples.en: After my story, they asked "How did you measure success?" and I mentioned wait times.
examples.zh: 我讲完经历后，他们问「你如何衡量成效」，我提到了等候时间。

collocations: follow up with "How did you measure success?"

words.expression: what was your role in the team
words.lemma: what was your role in the team
words.enDefinition: A question asking what someone personally contributed to a team
acceptedEnVariants: what was your role in the team

examples.en: I described the rota when asked "What was your role in the team?" at the interview.
examples.zh: 面试时被问到「你在团队中负责什么」，我介绍了排班表。

examples.en: To answer "What was your role in the team?" I explained which meetings I led.
examples.zh: 回答「你在团队中负责什么」时，我说明了自己主持过哪些会议。

collocations: ask "What was your role in the team?"
answer "What was your role in the team?"
follow up with "What was your role in the team?"

words.expression: a specific instance comes to mind
words.lemma: a specific instance comes to mind
words.enDefinition: An expression introducing a particular event you have just remembered
acceptedEnVariants: a specific instance comes to mind

examples.en: I said "A specific instance comes to mind." Then I described the day we lost the bookings.
examples.zh: 我说「我想起一个具体例子」，然后讲了预订记录丢失的那一天。

examples.en: The student said "A specific instance comes to mind." Her example was from a group assignment.
examples.zh: 这位学生说「我想起一个具体例子」，接着讲了小组作业的经历。

collocations: say "A specific instance comes to mind."
begin with "A specific instance comes to mind."
respond with "A specific instance comes to mind."

words.expression: would you like me to elaborate
words.lemma: would you like me to elaborate
words.enDefinition: A polite question offering to give more detail about something
acceptedEnVariants: would you like me to elaborate

examples.en: I asked "Would you like me to elaborate?" after summarizing how the repair request was handled.
examples.zh: 我概述了维修请求是怎样处理的，然后问「您想听我展开说说吗」。

examples.en: My tutor suggested "Would you like me to elaborate?" after a brief answer about teamwork.
examples.zh: 导师建议，团队合作的话题简短回答后可以问「您想听我展开说说吗」。

collocations: ask "Would you like me to elaborate?"
say "Would you like me to elaborate on that?"
offer "Would you like me to elaborate on my role?"
